Paragraph:
Translation: A person who is not disturbed by the incessant flow of desires—that enter like rivers into the ocean which is ever being filled but is always still—can alone achieve peace, and not the man who strives to satisfy such desires.

Purport (Excerpt): Although the vast ocean is always filled with water... it remains the same—steady; it is not agitated... Desires may come to him like the waters of the rivers... but he is steady in his activities... Others, however, who fulfill desires even up to the limit of liberation... never attain peace.
Situation/Problem_Faced: The illusion that peace is achieved by satisfying every desire that enters the human mind.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna offers the famous Ocean Analogy: Rivers (desires) continuously pour into the ocean, yet the ocean never overflows or loses its calm baseline. A peaceful person lets desires pass through consciousness without reacting, whereas someone trying to satisfy every desire stays perpetually agitated.
Outcome/Resolution: The fundamental myth of consumer culture—that satisfaction comes from fulfillment of desires—is completely shattered.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.The 'Oceanic Mind': Remaining still and deep despite a constant inflow of thoughts
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Desire-Adaptation Treadmill: The futility of trying to achieve peace by satisfying endless cravings
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Non-Attachment to Thoughts: Allowing mental rivers to flow in without being agitated

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Samudram apah pravisanti yadvat (Like rivers entering the steady ocean)
Kama-kami (One who chases after the fulfillment of desires)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The devotee is spiritually full and complete, needing nothing from the material world. Though thoughts and physical demands pour into their mind like torrential rivers, they remain unmoved and tranquil like a deep ocean. True peace belongs to them, not to those frantically trying to quench material thirst.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This is a masterpiece of cognitive acceptance. Having desires enter the mind is natural and automatic ('rivers flowing into the ocean'). Mental illness and stress occur when we compulsively react to or attempt to satisfy every mental river. Peace comes from expanding your mental capacity to be like the ocean—noticing the thoughts without letting them agitate your depths.
